circuit:
* Sky130 5-bit switched-resistor DAC.
* 32 identical unit cells: unit resistor from vout to a CMOS driver that
* switches the far end between vdd and vss.  16/8/4/2/1 cells are driven by
* b4..b0 and one cell is tied low, so the conductance to vdd is code*G0 and
* the total conductance is 32*G0:  vout = code/32*VDD, Rout = R0/32 for all codes.
.subckt switched_resistor_dac_5bit vss b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 vdd vout

XIAtN nat vss vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.5 nf=1
XIAtP nat vss vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.5 nf=1
XIBtN dt nat vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.4 nf=1
XIBtP dt nat vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=4.2 nf=1
XRt dt vout vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=0.35 l=39.7

circuit:
* 5-bit non-inverting voltage-mode switched-resistor DAC (Sky130).
*
*   vout = (b0 + 2*b1 + 4*b2 + 8*b3 + 16*b4)/32 * VDD
*
* Binary-weighted switched-resistor array made of 32 identical unit branches.
* A unit branch is one unit poly resistor (vout -> x) in series with one unit
* CMOS rail switch (x -> vdd for a '1', x -> vss for a '0').  Bit i owns 2**i
* unit branches; one extra unit branch is permanently tied low.  The array
* therefore always presents exactly 32 unit conductances from vout to the
* rails, 'code' of them to vdd and '32-code' of them to vss:
*
*     vout = VDD * code/32          Rout = Runit/32  (the same at every code)
*
* Every weight is an integer count of the same unit branch, so the switch
* on-resistance sits inside the unit and cancels out of the ratios instead of
* skewing them; it needs no trimming and tracks over PVT.  Rout is

circuit:
* 5-bit switched-resistor DAC for Sky130 (binary-weighted unit-element divider).
*
* Architecture
*   32 identical unit cells each switch one equal high-poly resistor between
*   vdd and vss and join it onto vout. Bit j drives 2^j cells; one dummy cell
*   is held in the code-0 state, so code k gives vout = k/32*vdd with a
*   code-independent output resistance Runit/32 (about 1.25 kohm). Supply
*   current is only vdd*x*(1-x)/Rout (zero at both end codes).
*
* Unit cell  in -> A -> B -> C -> rail switch -> Runit -> out  (non-inverting)
*   A  fast, P-strong input inverter (light load on the bit driver).
*   B  deliberately P-weak stage: its slow rising edge sits in the rising-bit
*      path and mirrors the weak P pull-up of the external two-stage bit
*      driver, cancelling the driver's rise/fall skew over PVT so rising and
*      falling legs switch together (small major-carry glitch).
*   C  strong switch-gate driver.
*   Rail switch: PMOS/NMOS widths ratioed so on-resistances stay matched
*      across temperature (keeps the mid-scale bow well under 0.05 LSB);
*      L=0.18 PMOS removes hot/FF subthreshold leakage (code-0 error, power).
*
* Bit-line loading is equalized with MOS gate capacitors so each bit input
* presents the same load as b4 (16 unit inputs) and all bits see identical
* driver delay.

.subckt sr_dac_unit in vdd vss out
* A: input inverter
XPA sa in vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.18 w=1.68 nf=1
XNA sa in vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.42 nf=1
* B: P-weak skew-compensation inverter
XPB sb sa vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.18 w=1.4 nf=1
XNB sb sa vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
* C: switch-gate driver
XPC sc sb vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.18 w=5 nf=1
XNC sc sb vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2.5 nf=1
* rail switch: leg = in
XPS leg sc vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.18 w=9 nf=1
XNS leg sc vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.6 nf=1
* unit resistor (~40 kohm)
XRU leg out vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=0.35 l=39.24
.ends sr_dac_unit

.subckt switched_resistor_dac_5bit vss b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 vdd vout
* b0: 1 unit + load equalization for 15 unit inputs
XU00 b0 vdd vss vout sr_dac_unit
XCP0 vdd b0 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.18 w=25.2 nf=1
XCN0 vss b0 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=6.3 nf=1
* b1: 2 units + load equalization for 14 unit inputs
XU01 b1 vdd vss vout sr_dac_unit
XU02 b1 vdd vss vout sr_dac_unit

XCN1 vss b1 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=5.88 nf=1

XU05 b2 vdd vss vout sr_dac_unit
XU06 b2 vdd vss vout sr_dac_unit

XCN2 vss b2 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=5.04 nf=1

* 5-bit switched-resistor DAC (unit-leg, voltage mode).
* 32 identical unit legs (CMOS switch + high_po resistor) drive vout: bit i
* switches 2^i legs between vdd and vss (31 legs) and the 32nd leg is held
* at vss, so vout = code/32 * vdd with Rout ~ Rleg/32.
*
* Glitch control: every leg is driven through four inverters. The middle
* two are replicas of the external two-stage bit driver placed at opposite
* parity (per-bit stage-1 replica with the same device sizes and 48 um fanout,
* per-leg stage-2 replicas with the same P:N ratio), so the driver's rise/fall
* asymmetry cancels over PVT and legs turning on and off switch together.

* Per-leg stage-2 replica + output switch + resistor.
.subckt dac_leg vss n vdd vout
XN5 c n vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1 nf=1
XP5 c n vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2 nf=1
XN6 leg c vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.2 nf=1

circuit:
* 5-bit non-inverting voltage-mode switched-resistor DAC.
* Binary-weighted resistor bank summed at vout, with a unit termination
* resistor to vss.  Physical Sky130 high-resistance poly resistors are used
* as 2^i parallel unit cells per leg so the conductance weights are exact
* integer ratios.  Each leg is driven by a CMOS inverter whose p/n device
* widths are scaled with the leg resistance so the switch on-resistance is
* a fixed fraction of the leg resistance (keeps INL/DNL ratiometric).
.subckt switched_resistor_dac_5bit vss b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 vdd vout

* ---- bit complement generators (b_i -> nb_i) ----
XIP0 nb0 b0 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.67 nf=1
XIN0 nb0 b0 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.42 nf=1

circuit:
* 5-bit unit-element switched-resistor DAC (non-inverting, voltage mode).
* 32 identical res_high_po unit resistors share vout. Bit i owns 2^i unit
* cells (pre-driver inverter -> CMOS switch -> unit resistor) that drive their
* resistors to vdd when the bit is 1 and to vss when it is 0; one termination
* unit is held on vss. Vout = VDD*k/32 with Thevenin resistance R_unit/32.
* Switch widths balance PMOS/NMOS on-resistance across PVT (L=0.18 PMOS keeps
* hot/FF leakage low). The high-threshold pre-driver cancels most of the input
* buffers' rise/fall skew; b3 and b4 get stronger pre-drivers so the MSB side
* switches first on major carries, which keeps the carry glitch between the
* two commanded levels. Dummy gate caps equalise the load on every bit input.

XPDN0_0 nb0 b0 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.42 nf=1

* 5-bit non-inverting switched-resistor (binary-weighted conductance) DAC.
* Code k = sum(2^i * b_i) gives vout = k/32 * vdd.
* Per bit i: a unit PMOS/NMOS switch pair (2^i parallel units) selects vdd or
* vss into 2^i parallel unit resistors, so every branch is exactly R_U/2^i
* and the network Thevenin resistance is R_U/32 at every code.
* Only Sky130 PDK subcircuits are used; nodes xa*/xb*/nb* are private.
.subckt switched_resistor_dac_5bit vss b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 vdd vout
XIP0 nb0 b0 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=8 nf=1
XIN0 nb0 b0 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.5 nf=1
XIP1 nb1 b1 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=16 nf=1
XIN1 nb1 b1 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1 nf=1
XIP2 nb2 b2 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=32 nf=1

XIP3 nb3 b3 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=64 nf=1
XIN3 nb3 b3 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=4 nf=1
XIP4 nb4 b4 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=128 nf=1
XIN4 nb4 b4 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=8 nf=1
* bit 0: weight 1 unit(s)
XPA0_0 xa0 nb0 vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.2 w=2.76 nf=1
XNA0_0 xb0 nb0 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1 nf=1
XRA0_0 xa0 vout vss sky130_fd_pr__res_xhigh_po w=1 l=19.1068

circuit:
* 5-bit switched-resistor DAC: 32-unit parallel-conductance divider.
* Each unit branch: rail-swinging CMOS leg driver + unit resistor R_u to vout.
* Bit i drives 2^i units (one scaled INV1->INV2 chain + one scaled resistor R_u/2^i);
* the 32nd unit is an always-low branch, so vout = k/32*VDD (k = input code).
* Monotonic by construction; only driver Ron *imbalance* affects INL (R_u >> Ron).
* Narrow unit resistors (w=0.5) keep poly/STI parasitic cap (~w^2 at fixed R) low
* so the 1 pF load dominates and 1-LSB steps settle well inside the 5 ns code slot.
* beta=0.055 boosts the always-low branch R: a pure gain term (k*beta/32 LSB)
* that offsets the sampling-instant settling lag of the final ramp code.
* unit R = 44000.0 ohm (res_high_po w=0.5 l=64.7755)

* static-CMOS 5-to-32 decoder.  Ratiometric: the selected tap switch carries no

* size vary with tap height so that (tap impedance + switch Ron) stays bounded at
* every code, off-state subthreshold leakage stays negligible, and every switch

circuit:
* 5-bit switched-resistor DAC (voltage-mode string DAC).
*
* Topology: 32 matched poly resistors in a string between vdd and vss
* give 32 equally spaced taps (tap k = k/32 * VDD).  A one-hot
* multiplexer steers the addressed tap to vout.
*
* Decode race control: the complementers are NMOS-heavy (fast output
* fall, slow output rise) so on an up major-carry the ~bit lines of the
* falling bits rise well after the ~bit line of the rising bit has
* fallen, and on a down major-carry the falling bits deselect the old
* tap before the slow ~bit rise can select the new one.  The NAND5
* selects through a 5-series NMOS stack (slow, graded) but deselects
* through 5 parallel PMOS (fast), which low-pass filters any residual
* skew window.  Every code change is break-before-make.
*
* Switch sizing is tapered with tap voltage: a rail-driven NMOS is
* strong only for taps well below VDD-Vth(body effect) and a PMOS only
* for taps well above |Vth|.  The taper therefore uses NMOS-only
* switches for the lower taps, PMOS-only for the upper taps, and
* heavily wide lvt devices in parallel around mid-rail where both
* ordinary devices are body-effect weakened.
*
* Geometry: string unit 6.5/1.8 um x32, NAND5 0.84,
* complementer 2.5N/0.84P, invA 1.0N/2.0P,
* invB 3.0N/6.0P.

* ---------------- local standard cells (flat, not nested) ----------------
* NMOS-heavy inverter: fast output fall, slow output rise.
.subckt srdac_invn a y vdd vss
XMN y a vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2.5 nf=1
XMP y a vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
.ends srdac_invn

* 5-input NAND, one gate per tap code.
.subckt srdac_nand5 a b c d e y vdd vss
XMN1 y a nx1 vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
XMN2 nx1 b nx2 vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
XMN3 nx2 c nx3 vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
XMN4 nx3 d nx4 vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
XMN5 nx4 e vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
XMP1 y a vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1
XMP2 y b vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.84 nf=1

circuit:
* 5-bit non-inverting switched-resistor voltage-mode DAC (Sky130 PDK only).
*
* Architecture: 32 identical unit cells.  31 cells are switched by the binary
* bit inputs (16 for b4 .. 1 for b0) and one cell is hard-wired low, so the
* vout node always sees exactly 32 equal unit conductances.  Each cell:
*
*   vdd -[PMOS sw]- na -[R_unit]- vout
*   vss -[NMOS sw]- na
*
* Both switch gates are driven by the cell's inverter output bn = ~b:
* b=1 -> PMOS on (unit pulls up), b=0 -> NMOS on (unit pulls down).
* A unit that moves between the rails never leaves the network, so the output
* impedance is code-independent, the ladder stays linear, and every code step
* is strictly positive by construction.
*
* The series switch on-resistance is kept ~2% of R_unit and the PMOS/NMOS
* switch sizes are balanced so Ron_p ~= Ron_n: then vout(k) = k/32 * vdd
* exactly, including both endpoints (code 0 = 0 V, code 31 = 31/32 vdd).
* R_unit ~40k puts the worst-case mid-code supply draw ~0.8 mW at 1.98 V
* while the output pole (Rout ~1.3k x 1 pF) settles in ~1.3 ns.
*
* Unit cell: pins (b vdd vss vout).  bn/bp/bpn/na are private nodes.
.subckt dac_unit b vdd vss vout
* 3-stage skewed delay chain b -> bpn for the PMOS switch gate.  The
* bit drivers' rising output edge leads the falling edge by ~60-80 ps, so at
* a major carry the incoming (turn-up) units would act ~100 ps before the
* outgoing (turn-down) units release, spiking vout toward a rail.  The chain
* is weak in the turn-on direction (min-size devices) and strong in the
* turn-off direction (2 um devices), delaying turn-on ~50-80 ps relative to
* turn-off so both edges of a carry arrive together.
XINP bn b vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2.0 nf=1
XINN bn b vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.0 nf=1
X2P bp bn vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.0 nf=1
X2N bp bn vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2.0 nf=1
X3P bpn bp vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2.0 nf=1
X3N bpn bp vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.0 nf=1
* rail switches (sources sit on their rail: constant VGS, deep triode)
* W's balanced so Ron_p = Ron_n ~ 815 ohm at tt/1.8/27 (~2% of R_unit).
* NMOS switch gate is the fast (single-inverter) node: turn-down is quick.
XSWP na bpn vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=4.15 nf=1
XSWN na bn vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.0 nf=1
* unit resistor (poly, ~40k).  Narrow (w=0.35) keeps the poly-substrate
* parasitic ~0.7 fF per unit (~23 fF total) so it cannot slow the output.
XR na vout vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=0.35 l=39.2
.ends dac_unit

.subckt switched_resistor_dac_5bit vss b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 vdd vout
* LSB
XU0a b0 vdd vss vout dac_unit
* b1 (weight 2)
XU1a b1 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU1b b1 vdd vss vout dac_unit
* b2 (weight 4)
XU2a b2 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU2b b2 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU2c b2 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU2d b2 vdd vss vout dac_unit
* b3 (weight 8)
XU3a b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU3b b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU3c b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU3d b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU3e b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU3f b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU3g b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU3h b3 vdd vss vout dac_unit
* b4 (weight 16, MSB)
XU4a b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU4b b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU4c b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU4d b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU4e b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU4f b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit
XU4g b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit

XU4p b4 vdd vss vout dac_unit
* fixed 32nd unit: permanently in the pull-down state (b = vss)
XUF vss vdd vss vout dac_unit
.ends switched_resistor_dac_5bit

* Five-bit voltage-mode DAC: physical resistor string and one-hot tap selection.
.subckt dac_inv in out vdd vss

* 5-bit non-inverting switched-resistor voltage DAC

* Dummy unit is permanently tied to VSS through the same NMOS path.

circuit:
* 5-bit non-inverting voltage-mode switched-resistor DAC.
* Target: vout = (k/32) * vdd for digital code k (b0 LSB .. b4 MSB).
*
* Topology: 32 identical unit resistors share a single internal node
* (vint).  31 units are binary-weighted (1,2,4,8,16) and connect to
* vdd when their bit is 1 or to vss when it is 0; a 32nd dummy unit is
* always referred to vss so the ratiometric denominator is 32.
* Every unit carries its own bit switch, so each unit sees the same
* series resistance and vint = vdd * k/32.
*
* Glitch control: a single series transmission gate between vint and
* vout is opened (blanked) while any input bit is still moving, so the
* load capacitor is isolated from the string during a code change and
* holds its previous voltage.  Unit-switch control edges are locally
* delayed so they can only move after blank is already at a solid rail;
* the blank pulse is wider than that delay plus the input bit skew, so
* the string only re-connects to vout on the settled code.  Because the
* blank device sits in the vout path it carries no DC current, and its
* Ron does not enter the static transfer.

* ------------------------------------------------------------------
* Static CMOS helpers
* ------------------------------------------------------------------
.subckt sky_inv a y vss vdd
XMP y a vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2 nf=1
XMN y a vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1 nf=1
.ends sky_inv

* Medium inverter for internal node drive.
.subckt sky_inv_m a y vss vdd
XMP y a vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=8 nf=1
XMN y a vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=4 nf=1
.ends sky_inv_m

* Large inverter sized to drive a bank of unit-switch gates.
.subckt sky_inv_l a y vss vdd
XMP y a vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=16 nf=1
XMN y a vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=8 nf=1
.ends sky_inv_l

* Non-inverting high-current buffer (medium -> large).
.subckt sky_buf a y vss vdd
X1 a n1 vss vdd sky_inv_m
X2 n1 y vss vdd sky_inv_l
.ends sky_buf

.subckt sky_nand2 a b y vss vdd
XMP1 y a vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2 nf=1
XMP2 y b vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2 nf=1
XMN1 y a n1 vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2 nf=1
XMN2 n1 b vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=2 nf=1
.ends sky_nand2

* 5-bit non-inverting voltage-mode switched-resistor DAC.

* non-inverting push-pull stage so every leg sees a low, pull-up/pull-down
* balanced source; the PDK poly resistors set the 1:2:4:8:16 weights.

* Resistance law (unit cell = w=1 l=140, ~45.9k ohms nominal):

* 5-bit non-inverting voltage-mode switched-resistor DAC, Sky130 PDK devices.
*
* Six binary-weighted poly-resistor branches sum at vout.  Branch k carries
* bit k (k = 0 LSB .. 4 MSB) with conductance 2^k*G0; an always-connected
* branch with conductance G0 closes the sum so that
*     V(vout) = vdd * (b4*16 + b3*8 + b2*4 + b1*2 + b0) / 32.
*
* Each branch switch is an NMOS (to vss) in parallel with a PMOS (to vdd),
* both gates driven by the complement of the bit.  Sources sit on their own
* rail with the bulk tied to the source, so every device sees the full fixed
* gate overdrive and no body effect.  Switch width scales as 2^k, so each
* branch switch resistance is the same fraction rho of its branch resistance
* and divides out of the divider ratio.
*
* Unit resistor: sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po, w = 1 um, l = 29.6173 um  (U = 10000 ohm)
*   weff  = 1 - 0.001                    = 0.999
*   rhead = 345.8312/(0.999+0.1558)      = 299.4695 ohm
*   rbody = 325*(35.7185+0.247)/0.999    = 11700.5 ohm
*   total = 12000 ohm nominal at 30 C
* Branch values: bit4 = 4||units = 3k, bit3 = 2|| = 6k, bit2 = 1 = 12k,
*   bit1 = 2 series = 2U, bit0 = 4 series = 4U, permanent = 4 series = 4U.
*   Sum of conductances = 8/U, so Rout = U/8 = 1250 ohm (x (1+rho)).

.subckt switched_resistor_dac_5bit vss b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 vdd vout

* 5-bit non-inverting voltage-mode switched-resistor DAC.
* Exact R-2R ladder built from 16 identical high-sheet poly unit resistors:
*   - 4 series R segments between ladder nodes n0..n4 (n4 = vout)
*   - five 2R legs, one per bit, switched between vdd (bit high) and vss
*   - 2R termination at n0, taken through a permanently-on NMOS so that the
*     termination leg carries the same switch resistance as a pulled-low leg

* driven by an internal inverter, so the single-ended bit input is sufficient.

circuit:
* 5-bit voltage-mode R-2R switched-resistor DAC (Sky130).
* b0 = LSB, b4 = MSB. Non-inverting; output = code/32 * vdd.
*
* R-2R ladder: series R between nodes n0..n4 (n4 = vout); each node has a
* 2R leg to a rail selector (PMOS switch to vdd when bit=1, NMOS switch to
* vss when bit=0); n0 is terminated with a fixed 2R to vss. Every ladder
* resistor is an identical sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po unit (a 2R leg is two
* units in series), so ratio accuracy comes from matching. The series units
* are marginally longer than the leg units so that a leg's 2R plus its small
* switch on-resistance still equals 2 series units, preserving the divider
* ratio with the rail switches closed.
*
* Each bit is driven break-before-make. A tapered 4-inverter chain makes a
* delayed, same-polarity copy bd of the bit; NAND(b,bd) drives the PMOS gate
* gp and NOR(b,bd) drives the NMOS gate gn. In steady state gp=gn=/b; during
* a transition both rail switches are off for the chain delay (~100-200 ps),
* which prevents vdd->vss shoot-through and lets the switching leg float
* (its 2R then briefly terminates the node) instead of being hard clamped
* to mid-rail, suppressing the major-carry glitch.
*
.subckt dac_bit vss vdd b s
* ---- delayed same-polarity bit bd (4 tapered inverters) ----
XD1A bda b   vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.5 nf=1
XD1B bda b   vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=0.75 nf=1
XD2A bdb bda vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=3 nf=1
XD2B bdb bda vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=1.5 nf=1
XD3A bdc bdb vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=6 nf=2
XD3B bdc bdb vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=3 nf=1
XD4A bd  bdc vdd vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=10 nf=2
XD4B bd  bdc vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=5 nf=1
* ---- NAND(b,bd) -> gp (PMOS gate): pmos parallel, nmos series ----
XNP1 vdd b  gp  vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=8 nf=2
XNP2 vdd bd gp  vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=8 nf=2
XNN1 gp  b  xnn vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=10 nf=2
XNN2 xnn bd vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=10 nf=2
* ---- NOR(b,bd) -> gn (NMOS gate): pmos series, nmos parallel ----
XOP1 vdd b  xop vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=12 nf=2
XOP2 xop bd gn  vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=12 nf=2
XON1 gn  b  vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=5 nf=1
XON2 gn  bd vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=5 nf=1
* ---- rail selector: PMOS pulls s to vdd when b=1, NMOS to vss when b=0 ----
XSP vdd gp s vdd sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=56 nf=8
XSN s  gn vss vss sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l=0.15 w=28 nf=4
.ends dac_bit

.subckt switched_resistor_dac_5bit vss b0 b1 b2 b3 b4 vdd vout
* ---- bit cells (delay + non-overlap gates + rail switches) ----
XB0 vss vdd b0 s0 dac_bit
XB1 vss vdd b1 s1 dac_bit
XB2 vss vdd b2 s2 dac_bit
XB3 vss vdd b3 s3 dac_bit
XB4 vss vdd b4 s4 dac_bit
* ---- switched 2R legs (two identical unit resistors each) ----
XRL0A n0 m0 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL0B m0 s0 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL1A n1 m1 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL1B m1 s1 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL2A n2 m2 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL2B m2 s2 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL3A n3 m3 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL3B m3 s3 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL4A vout m4 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRL4B m4 s4 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
* ---- LSB 2R terminator to vss ----
XRT0A n0 mt0 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
XRT0B mt0 vss vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.5
* ---- series R chain (n0 -> vout); slightly long to absorb switch R ----
XRS0 n0 n1 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.55
XRS1 n1 n2 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.55
XRS2 n2 n3 vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.55
XRS3 n3 vout vss sky130_fd_pr__res_high_po w=2 l=9.55
.ends switched_resistor_dac_5bit

* Vout = k/32 * VDD for code k (b0=LSB, b4=MSB)
* Topology: each bit steers a binary-weighted resistor between VDD and VSS.
* An inverter generates ~bi. PMOS switch connects Ri to VDD when bi=1.
* NMOS switch connects Ri to VSS when bi=0. A fixed R from Vout to VSS

* 5-bit thermometer-string switched-resistor DAC
* V_out = k/32 * VDD for code k = b4*16+b3*8+b2*4+b1*2+b0

* 32 transmission-gate switches select one tap

* Min-size switches minimize parasitic C on vout for fast settling

circuit:
* 5-bit voltage-mode switched-resistor (R-string) DAC.
* 32 unit poly resistors divide vdd..vss into 32 equal steps; a one-hot
* decoded transmission-gate mux connects tap k (k/32*VDD) to vout.
* Monotonic by construction; static accuracy set by unit-resistor matching.
* TG switches are tapered by tap: mid-string taps see the largest Thevenin
* resistance and get the widest devices; end taps stay small to minimize
* the off-switch capacitance that loads vout.
